BST260 Final Project Proposal

Wendi Yang

2026-11-17

Source: vignettes/proposal.qmd

To: BST260 Teaching Team, Fall 2026

Project overview

For my final project, I propose two analyses using public health datasets encountered in BST260. The first will investigate the association between body mass index (BMI) and systolic blood pressure among adults in NHANES. The second will describe patterns in reported waterborne disease outbreaks using the CDC dataset provided in the course package.

These analyses will apply tools from BST260 for data cleaning, descriptive statistics, visualization, and statistical modeling. I will present the work in two separate vignettes within the finalproject R package and publish the reports through a pkgdown website.

Analysis 1: BMI and systolic blood pressure in NHANES

Data source and provenance

I will use the NHANES dataset from the NHANES R package, which contains an educational adaptation of data from the 2009–2010 and 2011–2012 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles. NHANES is conducted by the National Center for Health Statistics and combines interviews with physical examinations.

I will document the package version, original data source, variable definitions, and steps used to construct the analysis sample. Because this dataset has been adapted for educational purposes, I will interpret the results as an exploratory classroom analysis rather than definitive national estimates.

Investigative objectives

My primary question is: How is BMI associated with average systolic blood pressure among adults aged 20 years and older?

I will also examine whether the observed association changes after accounting for age and sex. I expect higher BMI to be associated with higher systolic blood pressure, but the analysis will evaluate the pattern without assuming that the relationship is causal.

Variables and analysis plan

The primary variables will be BMI, average systolic blood pressure (BPSysAve), age, and the sex variable provided in the dataset.

I will first restrict the sample to adults aged 20 years and older and summarize missingness in the selected variables. I will report the number of participants included and excluded at each step.

Descriptive analyses will include means, standard deviations, medians, and interquartile ranges for continuous variables, along with counts and percentages for categorical variables. Histograms and boxplots will show variable distributions, and a scatterplot with a smooth curve will describe the relationship between BMI and systolic blood pressure.

I will fit a simple linear regression of systolic blood pressure on BMI, followed by a model adjusting for age and sex. I will report estimated differences in systolic blood pressure per five-unit increase in BMI. Model diagnostics will assess linearity, unusual observations, and residual patterns. Any uncertainty estimates will be interpreted in light of the dataset’s educational resampling.

Anticipated limitations

This is a cross-sectional analysis, so it cannot establish temporal order or causation. Blood pressure may also be influenced by medication use, diet, physical activity, and other factors not included in the primary model. Missing data may affect the composition of the analysis sample. A future extension would use original NHANES files and appropriate survey methods to obtain population-level estimates.

Analysis 2: Patterns in reported waterborne disease outbreaks

Data source and provenance

I will use the CDC waterborne illness dataset distributed as waterborne in the finalproject package. Before analysis, I will review its documentation and original CDC source to establish the reporting period, unit of observation, variable definitions, and surveillance coverage.

I will document the dataset version, source URL, available years, and all cleaning or aggregation steps. I will also check whether each row represents an individual outbreak or an aggregated surveillance record before calculating summaries.

Investigative objectives

My primary question is: How do the number of reported waterborne disease outbreaks and their associated illness burden vary over the available reporting years?

A secondary question is whether outbreak frequency and illness burden differ across reported etiologies or water exposure categories, depending on the variables available.

Variables and analysis plan

I will examine reporting year, outbreak counts, illness counts, and available categories describing the cause or type of water exposure.

I will begin by reviewing variable types, missing values, duplicate records, and category labels. I will distinguish missing or unknown values from true zeros and identify potentially incomplete reporting years.

I will summarize reported outbreaks and illnesses by year. If outbreak-level illness counts are available, I will also describe the distribution of outbreak size using the median, interquartile range, and range.

Line plots will show annual patterns, while bar charts will compare categories. I will distinguish categories that account for many reported outbreaks from those associated with a large total number of illnesses. These will be descriptive comparisons; I will not calculate population incidence rates without appropriate denominators.

Anticipated limitations

Surveillance data capture reported events and may miss outbreaks that are not detected or reported. Differences across years or categories may reflect surveillance practices, reporting delays, or diagnostic changes as well as underlying disease patterns. Large outbreaks may dominate total illness counts. Therefore, I will describe patterns in reported outbreaks without interpreting them as direct measures of individual risk.

A future extension could incorporate population or exposure denominators and investigate changes in reporting completeness.

Reproducibility and final deliverables

The final project will include two analysis vignettes, documented data sources, reproducible R code, descriptive tables, figures, and discussions of findings and limitations. I plan to use tidyverse tools for data preparation and visualization and base R functions for regression.

The public GitHub repository will contain a valid R package with the required dependencies declared in DESCRIPTION. I will build and check the pkgdown website so that both analysis reports are accessible through GitHub Pages.
